speckit-cli-notifications: Two products share one release list and must never be confused
Update checks are throttled, skippable, and never noisy on failure

FR-001.title: Notification offers Update, View Changelog, Skip, Update first
tests: ahead of View Changelog and Skip

FR-002.title: Update installs exactly the offered version
tests: src/speckit/updateChecker.test.ts::installs the offered version and reloads when the reload is accepted

FR-003.title: A successful install offers a window reload
tests: src/speckit/updateChecker.test.ts::installs the offered version and reloads when the reload is accepted
leaves the window alone when the reload is declined

FR-004.title: A failed install opens the extension page
tests: src/speckit/updateChecker.test.ts::opens the extension page when the gallery does not have the version yet

FR-005.title: View Changelog and Skip keep their behavior
tests: src/speckit/updateChecker.test.ts::opens the offered version's own release
opens nothing when the user skips

expectations: Auto-updating without the developer pressing a button
context: constraint: update checks stay throttled, skippable and quiet on failure
intent: The new-version notification can install the new version
approach: Add an Update button that installs the offered version, offers a reload, and opens the extension page when the install fails

T001.did: Update button installs the offered version, offers Reload Window, opens the extension page on failure

T002.did: Button order, update plus reload, declined reload, failed install opens page, dismissal; two existing tests updated for the new first button

T003.did: Getting-started and changelog say the notification can update the extension

decisions.decision: Install the offered version pinned as id@version
decisions.why: a gallery that does not serve the version yet rejects it, which is the signal to open the extension page
decisions.rejected: installing latest, which succeeds silently as a no-op when the Marketplace lags

decisions.decision: Read the extension id from the running extension
decisions.why: matches the existing rule of not hardcoding the id

decisions.decision: Update installs by bare id, not id@version
decisions.why: VS Code pins an extension installed at a given version (installGivenVersion sets pinned), which turns its automatic updates off for good
decisions.rejected: the pinned id@version install the issue suggested for detecting Marketplace lag

implement.summary: The new-version notification offers Update, which installs the offered version and offers a reload
